configured_contact_search.near_branch_condition: travel >= near_start_travel OR normal_force >= 0.3 N OR force_norm >= 0.3 N
configured_contact_search.stable_contact_condition: normal_force >= 0.5 N OR force_norm >= 0.7 N continuously for 0.08 s

derived_deceleration_check.interpretation: The measured 2.400 mm travel between sustained near-branch selection and the sustained contact-condition window is close to the configured-speed deceleration distance. This supports late braking into contact as a major contributor to the initial force overshoot.
limitations: The TP source and RTDE actual TCP velocity/pose are available, but native speedl command samples are not directly recorded in command_timeline.jsonl.
The 10.651 N contact-search/settle maximum and 10.526 N baseline diagnostic maximum cover different phase windows and must not be conflated.
This identifies a strong contact-acquisition mechanism; it does not by itself prove that the same mechanism fully explains the later 0.5 s baseline release-gate failure.

evidence_boundary: Kunwei-derived force feedback and synchronized RTDE/TP telemetry; no independent task-force truth; no complete Figure-eight PATH; no motion rerun performed during this diagnostic.
